voiceover: Inside every living cell is a code. DNA isn't just a molecule. It's information — written in a four-letter alphabet, spelling out the instructions to build and run a living thing. In a single human cell: three billion letters, in exactly the right order, packed into a space far too small to see. Now, be fair to the science. Real progress has been made — the famous Miller-Urey experiment showed some of life's building blocks can form on their own. But building blocks aren't a living cell. The astonishing part is the coded information itself — the instructions in the very first self-replicating cell. And here is what we know from every case we can observe: coded information — a language, a program, a written message — traces back to a mind. So the code at the root of all life points to a mind behind it. The first cell didn't only need chemistry. It needed a message. As the psalmist wrote, long before anyone had seen a strand of DNA: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
